lessons.title: Define labels with examples
lessons.text:
Text labels encode a task definition, not access to a person’s inner state. A transparent keyword baseline reveals ambiguities before complex models are introduced. Preserve negation and route conflicting evidence to review rather than forcing a convenient class.

Make review an allowed outcome and distinguish requests from issues. Inspect the supplied input before using any tool. Write the decision rules in your own words and calculate one small result independently. The reference output is an answer key for this deliberately bounded fixture, not proof of general capability.

Policy for this project: Token match refund => request and broken => issue. Both or neither => review. This brittle baseline is educational, not a reliable sentiment or emotion detector.

For learners across regions underserved or excluded by mainstream providers: verify country eligibility, language, account/identity requirements, data terms, cost, quota and connectivity before choosing a cloud service. Use only legitimate available alternatives; never bypass restrictions or invent a country/account. No service access? Complete the labelled manual/fixture route without claiming a live AI run.

lessons.title: Trace a keyword baseline
lessons.text:
Text labels encode a task definition, not access to a person’s inner state. A transparent keyword baseline reveals ambiguities before complex models are introduced. Preserve negation and route conflicting evidence to review rather than forcing a convenient class.

Show exactly which tokens produce each label. Establish a baseline before changing prompts or code. Keep the original input immutable. Record expected values, observed values and whether each comparison passed. If the expected file conflicts with a justified policy, investigate rather than forcing a convenient match.

Policy for this project: Token match refund => request and broken => issue. Both or neither => review. This brittle baseline is educational, not a reliable sentiment or emotion detector.

MANUAL BASELINE / compare every named field
{
  "labels": [
    "request",
    "issue",
    "review",
    "review"
  ],
  "review_count": 2
}
Keep a separate observed-result column; the answer key is not a model response.

Keep tokenisation and decision rules separate. Build one inspectable transformation or bounded AI prompt. Keep calculation and validation deterministic where possible. lessons.title: Attack ambiguity and negation
lessons.text:
Text labels encode a task definition, not access to a person’s inner state. A transparent keyword baseline reveals ambiguities before complex models are introduced. Preserve negation and route conflicting evidence to review rather than forcing a convenient class.

Record failures rather than hiding them behind a high average score. Change one assumption at a time and predict the result first. Retain the failure, the revision and the rerun evidence. A failure is useful information: hiding a bad output or editing a test target after seeing the answer destroys the value of the experiment.

Policy for this project: Token match refund => request and broken => issue. Both or neither => review. This brittle baseline is educational, not a reliable sentiment or emotion detector.

3. Try another language: abstain and obtain appropriate evaluation before use.

lessons.title: Compare a hosted model carefully
lessons.text:
Text labels encode a task definition, not access to a person’s inner state. A transparent keyword baseline reveals ambiguities before complex models are introduced. Preserve negation and route conflicting evidence to review rather than forcing a convenient class.

Use the same human-labelled set and do not infer emotion from a label. Review what the fixture cannot establish. Explain who owns the decision, where human approval is needed and which access or professional constraints remain. Do not describe a small educational success as production readiness, certification, legal compliance or a guarantee.

lessons.title: Ship an annotation and error guide
lessons.text:
Text labels encode a task definition, not access to a person’s inner state. A transparent keyword baseline reveals ambiguities before complex models are introduced. Preserve negation and route conflicting evidence to review rather than forcing a convenient class.

Deliver the label definitions, confusion examples and review policy. Deliver a reproducible bundle rather than a screenshot alone. Include inputs, rules, output, failure tests, a short README and residual limitations. Ask another person to follow the instructions if possible; self-review and actual external review must be labelled separately.

Policy for this project: Token match refund => request and broken => issue. Both or neither => review. This brittle baseline is educational, not a reliable sentiment or emotion detector.
lessons.example:
HANDOFF MANIFEST:
input.json — immutable source
expected.json — fixture answer key
actual.json — result actually observed
evidence-log.csv — baseline plus three changes
README.md — reproduction and access route
limitations.md — unresolved failures, rights, approvals and scope
Never bundle a credential.
